title: Four Fifteenth Air Force fighter groups, same eleven-month combat period: missions, claimed victories, escort losses and Italian stations
sourceCitation: Daniel L. Haulman, 'Measuring Up: A Comparison of the Mustang Fighter Escort Groups of the Fifteenth Air Force, June 1944-April 1945', Air & Space Power History 69(4), Winter 2022, printed p. 45 (PDF zero-based page 46), Table 1 and discussion pp. 45-48
formation: United States Army Air Forces, Fifteenth Air Force, fighter groups based in Italy

units.conflict: Table 1 records 66 escort missions encountering enemy aircraft, but prose later states 55 for 52nd. Keep table and alternate value, do not silently choose a single authoritative number.

units.squadronStrengthQualification: four squadrons for nine of eleven months
units.aircraftTypeQualification: P-51 for ten of eleven months

globalCautions: A 'mission' here is a GROUP mission, not one individual aircraft sortie; do not compare these group mission counts directly with national sortie totals.
The enemy aircraft 'aerial victories' are recorded USAAF CLAIMED/CREDITED victories, not matching independently verified German aircraft losses.

The bomber losses attributed to escort groups are NOT mutually exclusive: one bomber loss could appear against two fighter groups protecting the same bomber formation at different times or altitudes. DO NOT sum the four rows to get a theater bomber loss figure.

Escort-group mission losses are BOMBERS lost while that group was part of escort, not losses of the fighter group; fighter-group own loss information is supplied only indirectly in the printed credits-to-own-combat-loss ratio.
Italian base strings in the article are station NAME candidates without relocation dates or coordinates; must geolocate and date-verify before Atlas mapping.
The source article's interpretation and race-related comparisons should not be silently converted into causal assertions. Display comparable raw observations and their definitions only.
